contract.words: I want $5,000 collected within 30 days, only from work in the auto glass repair and replacement industry. I can put in up to $1,000 of my own money.

terms.proofCondition: first collected payment from an auto glass buyer

strategy.title: Month-one local SEO / Google Business Profile package sold to independent auto glass shops at $750, fulfilled by a subcontracted local-SEO freelancer
strategy.why: Verified evidence puts what small-market auto glass shops pay for SEO at $700-$2,000 per month (BizIQ, Jul 2026), so $750 sits at the bottom of the paid range; 7,047 US auto glass replacement businesses are listed (NAICS Association), so 7 buyers is a tiny share. Only $100 of the owner's money is put in before any buyer pays; the freelancer is paid from each shop's payment. What nothing records is the close rate on cold outreach, a freelancer committed at <= $199 per shop, and Stripe's first-payout timing, so the plan is conditional on a 10-day market test.

alternatives.title: Consumer windshield replacement brokered to a subcontracted mobile installer
alternatives.why: Retail price is evidenced ($393 average, Glass.com 2026) but no installer's wholesale price exists, so the margin and the paid-ad cost per job are unknown and 13 jobs would be needed.

alternatives.title: AI missed-call answering setup resold to auto glass shops
alternatives.why: Shops can buy the same tools self-serve from $49-$199/month, so a $300 setup premium is unevidenced, and 17 sales would be needed in 30 days.

alternatives.title: Exclusive windshield leads sold per lead (refused at admission)
alternatives.why: Glass.com sells exclusive leads around $29 while clicks for 'windshield replacement' cost $15-$30 each, so cost per lead exceeds price.

reviews.reasons: The plan treats as verified two figures the evidence gate rejected. The BizIQ '$700-$2,000 per month' is an SEO vendor's own description of monthly agency retainers, not a record of what independent shops paid for a one-off first-month package (claim rejected on verification); the NAICS 7,047 count has no year, does not separate independent shops, and gives no purchase frequency (rejected on scope). The card's revenueRange, price and buyerVolume are all RECOMMENDATION, and Brain's links mark OFFER_AND_PRICE and MARKET_VOLUME unestablished. As a CONDITIONAL plan it can still stand, but only if the test is what decides price, and it must not take shops' orders before a freelancer has committed in writing.
findings: Recomputed: 7 x $750 = $5,250 >= $5,000 collected; freelancer 7 x $199 = $1,393; setup $100; net $3,757. Peak exposure: $100 setup + $398 for the first two freelancer orders (Fiverr/Upwork are paid at order, day 12, before the day-17 Stripe settlement) = $498 <= $1,000. Second cohort receipts day 20 settle day 27 <= 30. Arithmetic of the ledger is consistent.

Price is not evidenced: q_price 'EVIDENCED' and 'Verified evidence puts what shops pay at $700-$2,000' are false - the card's revenueRange/price are RECOMMENDATION and the BizIQ claim was rejected as a seller's benchmark. Mark q_price as the test's unknown and add OFFER_AND_PRICE to validation.decides (two paid $750 invoices are what would establish it).

Buyer volume is not evidenced: q_buyers 'EVIDENCED 7,047' was rejected (no year, not limited to independents, no frequency). 600 reachable shops from map listings is the plan's actual reach; that list count is a step output, and MARKET_VOLUME should be in decides or measured by s1 before s3.

Order of tests: the freelancer quote (s2) is due by day 5, but offers go out from day 2 and the owner invoices from day 5; the plan can take buyers' orders before fulfilment is shown possible. Require the written <= $199 quote before s3 sends any offer.
The offer is a one-off month-one package, but the source range is a monthly retainer; even a passing test at $750 says nothing about recurring revenue - do not count any month two.
s1/s3 rely on SEND_A_MESSAGE, which is NOT_CONNECTED; the plan should say who sends (the owner's own inbox or the $100 tool) and the owner hours for it.

conditions.why: No EVIDENCE fact holds a price buyers paid; the only submitted source (BizIQ, an SEO vendor's typical monthly retainer) was rejected on verification as not a buyer-paid price for this one-off package.
The NAICS 7,047 count was rejected (no year, not independent shops, no purchase frequency); the card's buyerVolume is a RECOMMENDATION.

reviews.reasons: This revision correctly stops calling the BizIQ range and the NAICS count verified: price is now ASSUMED and measured by shops paying the $750 invoice, and OFFER_AND_PRICE is in validation.decides. The arithmetic carries: 2 paid of 150 (1.33%) on the 600-shop reach is 8 deals = $6,000 >= $5,000; 7 x $750 = $5,250 collected by day 27; peak exposure about $498 <= $1,000. But the test still takes buyers' orders before fulfilment is shown possible: s4 (owner invoices each shop that agrees, from day 5) depends only on s3, not on s2 (the freelancer's written <= $199 quote, due by day 5), and offers go out from day 2. A shop can agree and be invoiced before any freelancer has committed. Also, the 600 reachable independent shops are an estimate the plan does not measure.
findings: Make s3 (or at least s4) depend on s2: no offer sent, or at minimum no invoice issued, until a freelancer has quoted <= $199 per shop in writing. As written the stop rule 'stop selling before taking any order' cannot hold, because invoicing begins on the same day the quote is due.

Add MARKET_VOLUME to validation.decides (or measure it in s1): the threshold extrapolation needs 600 independent shops with reachable emails; q_buyers is an undated, rejected directory count. State the stop if s1 finds fewer than ~525 contactable shops (7 deals / 1.33%).
s1/s3 rely on SEND_A_MESSAGE (NOT_CONNECTED) and READ_REPLIES (UNREAD); name who sends and the owner hours if Brain cannot.

The cash ledger pays the freelancer for the first cohort on day 17 while delivery starts day 12; Fiverr/Upwork orders are paid at order, so that $398 leaves on day 12, before the day-17 settlement - still inside the $1,000 exposure cap, but the ledger should show it.

findings: Recomputed: 7 x $750 = $5,250 collected >= $5,000; freelancer 7 x $199 = $1,393; setup $100; net $3,757. Exposure: $100 (day 0) + $398 at order (day 12) before the day-17 settlement = $498 <= $1,000; the day-20 $995 is paid from the $1,500 already settled. strategy.title: Month-one local SEO / Google Business Profile package sold to independent auto glass shops at $750, fulfilled by a subcontracted local-SEO freelancer
strategy.why: An auto glass SEO vendor states its packages typically run $700-$2,000 per month (BizIQ, Jul 2026), so $750 is at the bottom of what sellers charge; the independent verifier rejected that as a buyer-paid price, and rejected the 7,047-entity NAICS listing as an undated, mismatched count, so price and volume are measured by the test itself (shops paying the invoice). Only $100 of the owner's money is put in before any buyer pays; the freelancer is paid from each shop's payment. What nothing records is whether shops pay $750, the close rate on cold outreach, a freelancer committed at <= $199 per shop, and Stripe's first-payout timing, so the plan is conditional on a 10-day market test. Only the one-off month-one package is counted; no recurring month two is assumed. The owner sends from the cold-email tool and reads replies himself (Brain's sending is not connected).

alternatives.why: Glass.com sells exclusive leads around $29 while clicks for 'windshield replacement' cost $15-$30 each, so cost per lead exceeds price.
